rationale: The golden solution is a faithful word-level recovery of the flattened netlist: tracing the gate logic shows the Moore state advances to a pulse state exactly one registered cycle after the '101' + '1' sequence is sampled, and the golden FSM reproduces this identical one-cycle latency. Yet evaluate.py's own harness rejects the golden on FR2 (9/30 mismatch on shipped stimulus), FR4 (12/65 mismatch on hidden random sequences), and SR3 (3/16 mismatch on adversarial sequences), and the vulnerable/naive baseline shows similarly-shaped but different mismatch counts rather than a clean pass/fail split. This pattern (consistent partial mismatches across every FR/SR that compares waveform behavior, on both golden and baseline) indicates a bug in the evaluator's own comparison harness or reference-simulation wiring (e.g. a clock-edge/sampling misalignment, an off-by-one in when it samples 'out' relative to driving 'in'/'rst', or a stimulus-file column/order misread) rather than a genuine behavioral defect in the golden RTL. Because the golden run fails, mutation_score is 0.0 and not meaningful, and coverage/discrimination cannot be trusted. Per the golden_rejected rule, this must be routed to evaluation_framework repair rather than case_artifacts, since the golden's interface and behavior conform to the pinned spec and design brief.
revision_instructions: The evaluate.py harness incorrectly rejects a submission that correctly implements the pinned interface `recovered_fsm(clk, rst, in, out)` and behaves as a proper Moore machine. Do not diagnose or fix this by inspecting any specific submission's internal state encoding or source text — the checks must be purely behavioral, driven through the pinned ports only. Concretely: 1) Re-verify the testbench's clock generation and edge-sampling order: drive rst/in on one clock phase and sample 'out' after the state-update edge has settled, consistently for both the reference (flattened_netlist.v + primitives.v) instance and the submission instance, so that both are sampled at the exact same simulation time relative to the same edge. A one-cycle or half-cycle misalignment between when the reference netlist's registered output settles and when the submission's output is captured would produce exactly this kind of partial, non-zero mismatch count on every FR/SR check. 2) Re-check parsing of inputs/stimulus.txt: confirm which column is 'in' and which is the expected 'out', and confirm the harness applies rst for the correct number of leading cycles as described in design_brief.md, not an assumed fixed reset length that differs from the actual reset protocol. 3) For FR4 and SR3, ensure the hidden random/adversarial stimulus generator drives 'in' to both the reference netlist instantiation and the submission instantiation on the identical set of clock edges (not via two separately clocked always blocks that can drift), and that comparison happens after both DUTs have had their outputs registered for that same edge. 4) After fixing alignment, all requirement checks must still fail-on-presence for banned primitive instantiation (SR1) and fail if the port list deviates from the pinned interface (SR2), and must otherwise judge PASS/FAIL solely from simulated 'out' waveform equality with the reference netlist — never from source-text similarity to any reference implementation. Re-run against the golden solution: it must produce all [TEST] PASS lines with zero mismatches before mutants are regenerated and mutation testing is meaningful.
